summary:
Utah restricts restroom and locker-room use by sex assigned at birth in public schools and government-owned buildings. HB 257, titled Sex-based Designations for Privacy, Anti-bullying, and Women's Opportunities, was introduced on 11 January 2024 and signed by Governor Spencer Cox on 30 January 2024. The statute does not reach private businesses, so hotels, gyms and commercial venues fall outside it. New government buildings must include single-occupant facilities. A person facing a complaint may answer it with documentation: a birth certificate and, where the marker on that certificate has been changed, proof of gender-affirming surgery. The defence rests on records a visitor will generally not carry, and the law provides no alternative route for someone whose documents were issued outside the state.

Enforcement runs through complaints rather than police action. A reporting form allows residents to report transgender people in privacy spaces such as changing rooms and restrooms, and complainants may choose whether their own names are included while the state investigates each reported violation. A procedure adopted in May 2024 allows officials and individuals to file formal complaints about suspected incorrect bathroom use in schools and government buildings. The ACLU of Utah opposed HB 257 on the ground that it invites discriminatory enforcement.

In March 2025 Utah enacted a ban on LGBTQ pride flags in public schools and government buildings. A May 2025 account places the signing on 7 May and describes Utah as the first state to prohibit such flags explicitly, with fines of $500 a day. Salt Lake City adopted the Sego Visibility Flag, modelled on the transgender pride flag, as an official city flag in May 2025. Utah Pride's executive director said the state leads the nation in anti-LGBTQ legislation.

Gender-affirming care for minors is banned. The ban passed the House on 26 January 2023 and the Senate 20-8 the following day, and was signed on 28 January 2023 with immediate effect; treatment already under way in January 2023 could continue. Clinicians may provide care to patients under 25, but those patients hold a retroactive right to disaffirm consent and sue. A legislative legal review found the ban potentially unconstitutional for targeting transgender people. A two-year systematic review commissioned under the ban and released in May 2025 concluded that the treatments are effective for mental health and psychosocial outcomes and for body changes consistent with an affirmed gender, and safe with respect to bone density, cardiovascular risk, metabolic change and cancer; the legislature dismissed the findings and kept the ban in force.

State-issued identity documents remain amendable. A transgender person may change the gender marker on a Utah birth certificate on submission of a certified court order changing name and gender; surgery is not required, and an X descriptor is available subject to judicial approval. In May 2021 the Utah Supreme Court held 4-1 that judges must grant sex and name changes when the clinical requirements are met.

Nondiscrimination protection is partial. SB 296, passed in 2015, bans discrimination based on gender identity in employment and housing but not in public accommodations, and exempts religious organisations and their affiliates, including schools and hospitals. The hate-crime statute amended in 2019 covers gender identity, carries enhanced penalties and requires the collection and publication of hate-crime statistics; those amendments passed the Senate 18-11 and the House 64-9, with Senate concurrence 22-3, and were signed on 2 April 2019.

Sports participation has been contested for several years. House Bill 11, barring transgender athletes from sports, athletics and the Olympics, passed in March 2022, was vetoed by Governor Cox on 22 March 2022, and was enacted over the veto to take effect on 1 July; on 19 August a judge partly reversed it and allowed transgender girls to be considered case by case for girls' sports in 2022-2023. On 3 October 2024 Southern Utah University and Utah State University forfeited matches against San Jose State University during litigation over a transgender player's eligibility. In 2024 the state also barred transgender students from university dormitories matching their gender identity, after a transgender woman was assigned to a women's dormitory at Utah State University.

Marriage equality reached Utah on 6 October 2014, after the Tenth Circuit affirmed a district ruling of 20 December 2013 striking the state's ban; the ruling displaced the 1995 non-recognition statute H.B. 366 and the 2004 constitutional amendment defining marriage as the union of a man and a woman, which voters approved 65.8 per cent to 33.2 per cent. Adoption follows from the recognition of the marriage. Foster care and adoption are otherwise limited to married or single persons, with cohabiting unmarried couples barred and priority given to married couples under 1998 H.B. 103. For couples using in vitro fertilisation, parental recognition of the non-genetic, non-gestational parent follows only from marriage. In August 2019 the Utah Supreme Court held the bar on same-sex surrogacy agreements unconstitutional.

Private consensual sexual conduct is not criminalised. The state's sodomy statute was invalidated by Lawrence v. Texas in 2003 and repealed by the legislature in 2019, following House approval 74-0 with one abstention on 29 January, Senate approval 25-2 with two abstentions on 22 February, and signature by Governor Gary Herbert on 25 March 2019. Earlier changes had reduced the offence from a felony to a misdemeanour in 1969 and created an exemption for married couples in 1973.
tangentialFactors:
Two neighbouring states moved in the same direction on flags: Idaho and Montana signed comparable bans on LGBTQ pride flags at public buildings in 2025, while Boise made the pride flag an official city flag. The pattern is not uniform across the region, since municipal counter-measures exist inside states that restrict the symbol.

Within Utah the two restrictive instruments differ in how they bite. The flag prohibition carries a financial penalty of $500 a day, while the facilities law operates through complaints filed by officials or private individuals and is supported by a public reporting form, with the documentary defence turning on records held by the person complained about.
localsOnly:
Utah's corrections system is a documented site of harm for transgender prisoners. A March 2024 investigation by the U.S. Department of Justice found that the Utah Department of Corrections discriminated against an inmate by denying gender-affirming hormones.

Conversion therapy on minors is prohibited by an executive order issued by Governor Gary Herbert on 21 January 2020 and codified by legislation in February 2023. The prohibition covers LGBT minors but exempts clergy, religious counsellors, parents and grandparents unless they are acting as psychologists.

Schools operate under anti-bullying legislation in place since 2006, with parental notification added in 2013 and administrative Rule 277-613 covering sexual orientation. University of Utah employment policy has protected against discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation since 1991, was extended to faculty duties in 1996, to student rights in 1997 and to admissions in 2009, and Salt Lake City ordinances adopted in 2009 and 2010 cover employment and housing.

Two further state measures apply to residents. A March 2020 law bars personalised vehicle plates carrying offensive references to sexual orientation, and consumer privacy legislation effective 31 December 2023 explicitly includes sexual orientation.
outOfScopeNotes:
No data on the number of complaints filed under HB 257 or through the reporting form, or on their outcomes, appears in the sources for this record; the mechanism is documented, its use is not.

Whether the documentary defence in HB 257 can be met by a visitor holding documents issued outside Utah is not addressed by any Utah source consulted. Nor is it established how the state's own gender-marker rules interact with federal passport and visa marker rules for incoming travellers.

The flag ban is dated inconsistently: one source places a ban in March 2025, another reports the signing on 7 May 2025. Whether the state prohibition covers a city's own official flag, including the flag Salt Lake City adopted in May 2025, is not resolved by the sources.

A legislative legal review found the 2023 care ban potentially unconstitutional for targeting transgender people, and the review's later treatment in litigation is not sourced here. The hate-crime statute requires the collection and publication of statistics, but no gender-identity-specific figures for Utah were located.

No Utah-specific data on violence against transgender people was identified in the sources used for this record.
